Whether this activity facilitates parallel pricing coordination remains uncompiled: tacit/express agreement between qualifying owners, reasonably interchangeable residential units, pricing conduct and affordability-control exception require evidence and legal review. Parallel prices alone do not establish agreement.

The actor must be the qualifying owner or its agent, representative or subcontractor, and the identified service provider must satisfy the operative coordinator/software-or-device/coordinating-function definition and scoped exclusions. Owner units and a service action do not settle these uncompiled relationships and legal qualifications.

The algorithmic-device and coordinating-function exclusions have not been compiled for this services transaction. They include qualifying non-AI spreadsheets requiring human analysis, query-only databases, research/statistical analysis/testing without lease-setting use, free public rent estimates, qualifying brokerage databases, and lawful government affordability-control activities. These are definitional limitations, not blanket exemptions from other prohibited conduct.
